correctness.rationale: Factoring the common character reduces every two-frequency idempotent to \(1+e_N(dx)\). With \(g=\gcd(d,N)\) and \(L=N/g\), the denominator is exactly \(2gS_L\), while the target numerator is controlled by a unit residue modulo \(L\). Reducing units from \(L\) to \(L/\gcd(a,L)\) shows the maximum absolute cosine occurs at the residue classes \(\pm1\), giving the divisor-and-gcd formula. The finite cosine sums evaluate to the stated cosecant/cotangent forms. A fresh brute-force check over every target for \(2\le N<15\) agreed with the closed formula.
